title: Items on belts are now drawn: every piece at its real sub-tile position, every belt coloured by whether it is starved, flowing, saturated or jammed, and the inserter arms visibly swinging

verified.pixel proof: item surface hidden vs show: 17368 px changed against a 3368 px renderer-noise floor (mean 6.016 vs 1.388)
verified.pixel proof: belt-state surface hidden v: 22816 px changed against a 5156 px noise floor (mean 7.234 vs 1.200)
verified.all four flow states present in one fram: 13 starved / 9 flowing / 11 saturated / 11 backed-up belt tiles
verified.mutation: LcnItemLayer._draw returns imm: the item pixel proof goes red (see report)
verified.draw cost, 2013 items in flight, all 201: item surface 2845 us/frame, all three surfaces 4652 us/frame (1.41 us per item)
verified.sample cost, same factory: 8918 us/tick, dominated by items_for_view() allocating one Dictionary per item

open: [P03] logistics: there is no machines_for_view(). Arms, splitters and underground pairs are read READ-ONLY off logi.world.inserter_ids / splitter_ids / entities because nothing publishes them. One accessor would close that.

[P03] logistics: items_for_view() allocates a Dictionary per item and costs ~4.4 us per item — 8.9 ms/tick at 2013 items, the single largest cost in this part. A packed variant (PackedVector2Array positions + PackedInt32Array kinds) would cut it several-fold.

INTEGRATOR / game/core/ui_layers.gd: there is no row for world-space simulation paint that must sit between [P13]'s entity pass and [P15]'s world juice. This part took LcnLayers.WORLD (0) with z 1/3/4, which is the closest existing entry; if a row is wanted, it is not this part's file to add.
[P19] overlays: the logistics lens (F5) now duplicates part of this always-on read. Worth deciding whether the lens should become the detail view rather than a second belt tint.
perf was measured on shared, contended cores under llvmpipe software GL with other agents building at the same time — the integrator's single-run number is the one to trust.
